one_line: Short AI LABS walkthrough of ChatGPT's web search for Plus users, with cited sources, live stock and flight queries, and a Chrome extension that routes browser searches to ChatGPT.
summary: The host demonstrates ChatGPT's web search feature, available from the web button for Plus-plan users. Answers are built from multiple web sources, each paragraph carries a source reference, and the sources link out to the originals. The host tests a weather query, a GameStop stock query (showing price changes over day, month and year), and a flight search with booking links. A prompt then offers a Chrome extension that makes ChatGPT the browser's default search, and a local query ("best coffee shops near me") returns results with a map. The video is a feature tour with no benchmarks, accuracy checks or failure cases. The closing comparison notes that ChatGPT still trails Google in monthly visitors, which is shown on screen without figures.

key_ideas.idea: ChatGPT web search is available from the web button for Plus-plan users and offers suggested queries as you type.
key_ideas.detail: The feature is presented as a Google-style search inside ChatGPT, with a set of suggestions shown before the search runs.

key_ideas.idea: Answers are built from several web sources and each paragraph carries its own source reference.
key_ideas.detail: Clicking a source opens the original page, so the answer can be checked against the site it came from.

key_ideas.idea: Live-data queries return current results, and the host reads this as evidence the answers are up to date.
key_ideas.detail: A current-weather query was used to show freshness. This is a single demo, not a systematic test.

key_ideas.idea: Stock and flight queries return structured widgets with sources and booking links.
key_ideas.detail: The GameStop query shows price changes across day, month and year. The flight query lists results with sources and a path to book.

key_ideas.idea: ChatGPT offers a Chrome extension that makes it the default search from the browser address bar.
key_ideas.detail: The host installed it from the Chrome Web Store after a prompt appeared during a search. A local query returned results with a map.

key_ideas.idea: The host frames the release as a move toward an all-in-one assistant that competes with Google and Perplexity.
key_ideas.detail: This is the speaker's interpretation. The only evidence is a visitor-count comparison shown on screen with no figures quoted.

techniques.name: Run a cited web search in ChatGPT
techniques.how: Use a Plus account, click the web button in the composer, pick one of the suggested queries or type your own, then check the per-paragraph source references and open the linked sites to verify claims.
techniques.when: Quick factual or live-data lookups (weather, prices, flights) where you want a sourced answer and a way to verify it.

techniques.name: Make ChatGPT the browser's default search
techniques.how: When the prompt appears during a search, follow it to the Chrome Web Store, add the extension, then type queries in the address bar.
techniques.when: If you want address-bar searches to go to ChatGPT instead of Google. The video shows the flow but not the extension's permissions or settings.

hot_takes: The host says ChatGPT is trying to replace Google, but the same segment concedes that Google remains the most-used website.
The video is a demo with no accuracy, latency or failure cases, so 'replaces Google' is unsupported by anything tested.
The extension prompt is presented as a helpful feature, but it is an upsell to make ChatGPT the default search.

relevance.why: Per-paragraph source attribution in generated answers is a provenance pattern that relates to MemoryMesh's retrieval provenance, but the video shows only the consumer UI.
relevance.action: Compare per-paragraph source attribution with MemoryMesh provenance fields when designing answer citations.

relevance.why: Consumer search UI with no harness, checkpoint or agent-run content.
Product walkthrough with no engineering detail beyond the UI flow.
